was: USACE Melvern Lake park halfway along the south shore, on a point. 43 paved sites: 19 with 30-amp electric and water, 24 basic. Showers, flush and vault toilets, drinking water, a dump station, boat ramp and dock; the Tallgrass Heritage Trail starts here. Booked on recreation.gov for May 1-Sep 29. Generators are allowed on basic sites until 10 PM. --Claude
note: USACE Melvern Lake park halfway along the south shore, on a point. Boat ramp and dock; the Tallgrass Heritage Trail starts here. Generators are allowed on basic sites until 10 PM. --Claude

was: Jackson County reservoir park on K-16 west of Holton, office at 10975 K-16 Hwy. Hook-up loops are Deer Run (A/B/C, same-day only, with the shower house), Cedar Point at the lake end of the north-west loops, the South Side peninsula loop, and the long-term Buffalo Run loop (by phone), which also has primitive sites. Pay daily permits at the courtesy box inside the gate. --Claude

was: Sedgwick County park, 720 acres around the 258-acre Lake Afton, W of Wichita. RV camping in several areas around the shore (Fisherman's Cove by the observatory, Shelter #5 on Fellowship Cove, Cottonwood Grove), with electric at many sites, water at 16 and restrooms (three open in winter). No generators. Permits at the park office or kiosk; 14 days, then 5 days away, 56 days a year at most. Blue-green algae warnings in summer (call 316-660-1780). --Claude

was: Pratt County's lake park: gravel pull-through service sites on open ground west of the lake road, plus primitive camping in designated areas and overnight camping on fishing piers 2-21 (not pier 1); fire rings, dump nearby. Swimming and wading are prohibited, and motorboats are allowed only for no-wake fishing. --Claude

was: City of Atwood lake park on the south side of Lake Atwood, run with the Lions Club: hook-up sites on a gravel lot by the lake's south-east arm, with showers. Pick up the permit and the hook-up key at the Atwood Liquor Store, 402 Grant on US-36. --Claude
note: City of Atwood lake park on the south side of Lake Atwood, run with the Lions Club: hook-up sites on a gravel lot by the lake's south-east arm. --Claude

was: City of Sterling RV park on East Van Buren Street beside Sterling Lake: a gravel row of pads between the railroad and the park road, across the road and a treeline from the lake. Self-pay envelopes at the west RV entrance. --Claude

was: City campground at 1100 D Street in Washington's City Park; pay at the campground drop box or City Hall. --Claude
note: City campground at 1100 D Street in Washington's City Park. --Claude

was: Douglas County park around 185-acre Lone Star Lake, southwest of Lawrence, on the site of the 1930s CCC camp that built the dam (stone water tower and fireplaces remain). 62 campsites in wooded loops above the north shore, 19 with electricity; restrooms, swim beach, boat ramp, shelters and a rentable community building. Permits in person from the camp host, check or cash only; quiet hours 10 p.m. to 6 a.m.; up to two shelters and eight people a site. --Claude

was: City of Winfield fairgrounds on US-160 at 1105 W. Ninth, by the Walnut River, open for camping year-round outside events too. Open camping areas with about 150 50-amp services on hard surface plus 20/30-amp outlets, limited seasonal water, a year-round dump station; the 44-acre Pecan Grove to the south has limited electric. Restrooms close in winter. After 14 days, move between the fairgrounds and the Pecan Grove. --Claude

was: City of Arkansas City park on W. Lincoln Ave: a small open camping area with no marked sites around a gravel loop with two covered picnic tables, plus drinking water and a dump station (11/2024 camper). On a 72-hour permit, 5 days at most (city fee schedule, January 2026). The city's pages don't say how to register. --Claude

was: Small private park at 1004 Massachusetts Ave on US-50 in Kinsley: level concrete full-hookup pull-throughs in an overnight section, with a separate extended-stay section. No office on site; book by phone and pay at the self-serve envelopes. Railroad close by. CAMPER-REPORTED RATE: $38-45 a night in August-October 2025 (RV Life reviews); the park has no web page (2026-11-05). --Claude

was: City of Ellinwood's Wolf Pond & RV Park on the south side of US-56 (Santa Fe & Fritz), beside a small fishing pond and the grain elevator. Pay at the site or at the City Office, 104 East 2nd. Handy for Cheyenne Bottoms and Quivira. --Claude

was: Rocky Mountain NP campground in Moraine Park, the Big Thompson River meadow below the high peaks. About 236 sites in five loops, 46 of them electric; rigs up to 40 ft, many sites tent- or van-sized and many not level. Flush toilets, dump station, solar shower stalls (bring your own bag). Reservation only in summer, first come first served in winter, when it is the park's only open campground. Rangers may enforce keeping RV windows closed due to bears. --Claude

was: Roosevelt NF (Canyon Lakes RD) campground beside Hwy 14 in Poudre Canyon, ~43 mi west of US 287, ~7,800 ft, in open ponderosa pine with a view of Sleeping Elephant Mountain. The Cache la Poudre River runs across the highway, mostly through private land here. Length conflict (2026-10-28): the campground page gives parking lengths of 15-30 ft and says this older facility will not take larger RVs, but the forest's campground-status table lists a 20-ft maximum spur. --Claude Online photos show at least a few sites that can take a class-B or small class-C, but reviews say the sites are short and unlevel: have a backup plan. --AWH 2026-10-28

was: Crystal River valley 1.5 miles before Marble (Aspen-Sopris RD, White River NF); widely spaced sites, several at the river's edge, paved campground roads. Concession-run (American Land & Leisure). The group campground is 1/4 mile east. --Claude

was: Trailhead campground at 8,200 ft in a conifer-and-aspen grove at the East Marvine and Marvine trailheads into the Flat Tops Wilderness, 35 mi east of Meeker via Rio Blanco CR 8 and CR 12 (Blanco RD, White River NF). Corral sites for stock users sit outside the main campground; the creek is about 400 yards away. Cattle may graze in the area. --Claude

was: Small primitive campground near Pingree Park along the South Fork Cache la Poudre in lodgepole pine, elev ~9,000 ft; reached via well-maintained gravel Pingree Park Rd (CR 63E), passable by passenger cars. Length (2026-10-28): the campground page gives parking lengths of 15-25 ft and says this older facility will not take larger RVs; the forest's campground-status table lists a 20-ft maximum spur. At most a spur or two could take a 23-ft rig: have a backup plan. --Claude

was: Lodge, cabins and RV park on US-160 just east of South Fork, on the south side of the highway under the bluff, beside the Rio Grande National Forest; 30-amp back-in and 50-amp pull-through/back-in sites. River access is across the highway, not riverside. Also lodge rooms and cabins, hot tub, rec room with kitchen, trail up the bluff. --Claude

was: Family-owned RV park just north of Hwy 92, ~1.25 mi east of US 50/92 junction in Delta (adjacent to Safeway). Directory listings describe ~66 full-hookup sites, 30/50 amp, ~25 pull-throughs, big-rig friendly (long sites 45+ ft), so a 23-ft rig fits easily; the operator's site gives no counts. Pool, hot tub, game room, dog playpen, playground, propane sold on site; takes both overnight/transient and monthly stays. Cabins and tent camping listed as closed (2025). Near the Gunnison/Uncompahgre confluence but not on the water (Confluence Park ~2 mi). --Claude

was: Colorado River District campground and marina on Wolford Mountain Reservoir, 10 mi north of Kremmling on US-40. Four loops on a point in the reservoir: A-C electric, D non-electric; sites are not level, so bring levelers. Winter camping in Loop A only. Boat ramp, marina, swim beach. --Claude
